question:
Batch 74 = RULING 93 (orchestrator 2026-11-13 '23:59'), verbatim excerpts: "DEC-12d IS MEASURED PER CLIP, NOT PER CHANNEL ... THE RULE NOW: no channel is layout_ineligible by name. Every clip, any channel, is judged on its own frames by the pin-stage visual check ... The render's G10 stays as it is and runs on EVERY clip (not only has_chyron channels), still monitoring. The has_chyron flag stays in the registry as a hint that orders the check, nothing more. YOUR SIDE: G10 runs on every clip as a monitoring row; the vertical reframe must not cut a lower third mid-word where a wholly-in or wholly-out crop exists inside the face-safe range (measure on the published 0c68b589 CNBC clip ...; report whether a crop that keeps the speaker and clears the lower third exists)."
Measured (DoD 23:51): on that clip no full-height face-safe crop clears the lower third for the whole shot (a banner from 6.2 s); before the banner x 7-33 does (published 94).
The change:
- vertical_layout.py: Law-20 constants (LT_BAND 0.70-0.985 H, Canny 80/200, close 13x5, element height 14-90 px, min w 10 / area 60, FACE_MARGIN_FRAC 0.10); lower_third_spans(frame) -> word-sized element x spans in the band; single_crop(faces, spans, w, h): today's x (face-centred, as render_vertical) unless a crop edge falls inside an element; then the nearest x in the face-safe range [right + margin - cw, left - margin] (face boxes from the samples' area fraction) with no edge inside any element; else today's x, recorded cut. classify() stores each sample's spans ('lt') and, per single shot, crop_x + a 'lower_third' record (the spans of every sample of the shot: one static crop).
- render_vertical._shot_vf: uses shot['crop_x'] when it is an int inside [0, src_w - CROP_W], else today's face-centred x.
- qa_gates: g10_clip_ids(segments) = every talking head; run_all_gates passes it to the unchanged gate_g10 (G10_chyron stays MONITORING in release_auth; run_fresh uses run_gates' overall pass only as a report field).
- editorial_select.layout_eligible: no has_chyron exclusion (only a channel id needed); edl_rules R8 text (informational); test_editorial's DEC-12d test now asserts ruling 93.
- Tests: test_lower_third.py (8 pass; on the real published clip: the old crop cuts the tag; pre-banner the rule moves it into 7-33; whole shot: kept and recorded cut). 366 related tests pass; the 4 others need GPU0 or the worktree-absent v2f files, and the 3 GPU ones pass under the lease.
FIND: a path where the crop can now leave the face (or its margin) or exceed the frame; a clean clip (no lower third) whose crop changes; a layout class / shot boundary that changes (the protected references compare those); G10 becoming release-deciding; a crash path (no faces in a single shot, an unreadable frame, an empty band). Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

consensus_findings.issue: single_crop crashes on a 'single' shot with no detected faces: np.median of an empty list raises ValueError. The new classify line calls single_crop([f[0] for f in faces], ...) with no guard for an empty face list, so a faceless single-class shot aborts the whole layout pass instead of degrading to today's crop.
consensus_findings.evidence: shot["crop_x"], shot["lower_third"] = single_crop([f[0] for f in faces], spans, w, h)  # crop, every sample
consensus_findings.fix: Guard the empty case before calling single_crop (e.g. if not faces: shot["crop_x"], shot["lower_third"] = None, {"rule":"ruling 93","cut":False,"spans":len(spans)}), and/or make single_crop return (base, record) when faces is empty instead of calling np.median([]).

consensus_findings.issue: single_crop crashes on a single shot with no faces: np.median of an empty list raises, and the later min/max over faces also raises, so a no-face sample in a 'single' shot breaks classify
consensus_findings.evidence: cx = int(np.median([f[1] for f in faces]))  ...  left = min(f[1] - s / 2 for f, s in zip(faces, sides))
consensus_findings.fix: guard: if not faces, return (base, cut record) without the face-safe search

rejected_findings.issue: single_crop can return a face-unsafe crop: the face-safe range is clamped to [0, w-cw] but the margin constraint is not re-checked after clamping, so when the face box plus margin exceeds the frame the chosen x can leave the face (or its margin) or exceed the frame
rejected_findings.evidence: lo, hi = max(0, int(np.ceil(right + m - cw))), min(w - cw, int(np.floor(left - m)))
rejected_findings.fix: after clamping, verify lo<=hi and that the chosen x satisfies right+m-cw <= x and x <= left-m; else fall back to base

rejected_findings.issue: single_crop's face-safe range can be inverted (lo > hi) when the face box is wider than the crop, making clear empty and silently falling back to today's x even though a valid x may exist; also the range uses int(np.floor(left - m)) which can exclude the exact boundary x
rejected_findings.evidence: lo, hi = max(0, int(np.ceil(right + m - cw))), min(w - cw, int(np.floor(left - m)))
rejected_findings.fix: clamp lo to >=0 and hi to <= w-cw, and if lo>hi widen to the full [0, w-cw] range before the clear search

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: single_crop's face-safe range uses the face box side estimated as (area_fraction * w * h)**0.5, i.e. a square box, but the recorded face data is [area, cx, cy] with no aspect; if the detector's area fraction is of the full frame while the box is not square, the estimated left/right edges can be wrong, so the 'face-safe' range may not actually contain the face. The test's FACE = [0.04, 397, 358] gives side = sqrt(0.04*1920*1080) ≈ 288px, which the test comment itself calls 'box side ~288 px' — this assumes a square box, which is only valid if the detector's area fraction corresponds to a square. If the detector reports a non-square box's area fraction, the margin check in the test (FACE[1] - side/2 - x >= 0.10*CW - 1) passes only because the test's own side estimate matches the implementation's, i.e. the test is self-fulfilling, not evidence the face is actually safe.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: sides = [(f[0] * w * h) ** 0.5 for f in faces]  — assumes square boxes; FACE = [0.04, 397, 35]8 comment 'box side ~288 px'
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Store the face box's w/h (or aspect) in the samples' face records and compute left/right from the actual box, not the square-root-of-area heuristic; or document that the detector's area fraction is of a square-equivalent box.

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: lower_third_spans is called on every readable sample even when the shot class is not 'single' (stack2/stack3/screen/uncertain), wasting compute; more importantly, the 'lt' spans are stored per-sample in the output VERTICAL_LAYOUT.json, changing the protected reference's schema (new 'lt' key per sample, new 'crop_x'/'lower_third' keys per single shot). The audit question asks about 'a layout class / shot boundary that changes (the protected references compare those)' — the class/boundary logic itself is untouched, but the reference JSON comparison will fail on the added keys unless the reference comparison ignores extra keys.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: "lt": [list(s) for s in lower_third_spans(frame)] if ok else []  — added to every sample regardless of class
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Verify the protected-reference comparison ignores added keys, or gate the 'lt' computation to single-class shots only (both a perf and a reference-diff concern).

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: run_all_gates now calls g10_clip_ids(segments) unconditionally, but the old code only populated chyron_clip_ids when both edl_path and channels_json_path were provided (and swallowed errors). If segments is empty or lacks 'type' keys, g10_clip_ids returns an empty set — same as before — but if the EDL/registry files are missing, the new code no longer needs them, which is fine; the subtle change: the old code's chyron_clip_ids came from EDL channel→clip mapping, the new one from segment 'type'=='talking_head'. If a segment's 'type' field is absent (seg.get('type') == 'talking_head' is False), that clip silently loses G10 coverage where the old EDL-channel mapping would have caught it via the channel's has_chyron. Clips whose segments lack a 'type' key (or use a different type string) are now silently skipped by G10.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.evidence: return {seg["label"] for seg in segments if seg.get("type") == "talking_head"}
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Confirm every segment in the final manifest carries type=='tailing_head'... (typo: talking_head) for all talking-head clips; otherwise fall back to the EDL/registry mapping when the segment type is missing.
